terminologyProfile.domain: real-time procedural Three.js architectural hero prop
terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable procedural 3D terms and evidence-linked component or material fields.

objectClass.notes: Three admitted complementary views fix facade symmetry, nave depth, five-window side rhythm, rear-offset tower placement, roof intersections, and explicitly solar—not Christian—iconography.

reasoning: The identity silhouette combines a long nave, raised front gable, columned portico, rear-offset tower, tall slate spire, and radial sun finial.
The roof must be a closed solid gable volume with attached shingle relief, never two rotated box slabs.
The facade requires a segmented rose window, separate gold sun disc, twin lancets, recessed doors, four columns, pediment, and steps.
Ashlar, slate, lancets, buttresses, rose wedges, belfry arches, spire ribs, and sun rays require deterministic repeated systems.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Identity depends on a deep architectural hierarchy, two solar emblems, repeated stained-glass systems, and an attached multi-stage steeple.

detailInventory.note: Twenty observed identity systems are consolidated from the main, front, and side inventories; every item maps to a real local feature or material override.

details.description: Rear-offset tower, open belfry, dark spire, and finial.
Gold solar core with alternating radial rays and no cross.
Dark recessed arches between white piers.
Gold ribs and lower diamond lattice.
One closed nave gable prism with end caps.
Regular overlapping dark slate courses.
Offset white ashlar blocks with cool recessed mortar.
Gold central sun, rays, and saturated radial glazing.
Dark radial lead cames and perimeter ring.
Separate gold sun disc with pointed rays, never a cross.
Four tapered columns with plinths and capitals.
Closed shallow gable pediment with gold inner trim.
Four broad steps widen toward y=0.
Twin pointed stained-glass lancets flank the facade.
Five pointed lancets repeat along each nave side.
Gold suns and red, blue, violet, green glass divided by dark cames.
Gold bands trace eaves, pediment, and tower caps.
Projecting white piers divide nave bays.
Dark double doorway behind the portico.
Real stone chamfers catch the upper-left key.

definitionOfDone: The model reads immediately as the admitted fantasy sun temple from front, side, and three-quarter views.
Tall rear-offset steeple, dark solid spire, gold radial sun finial, white ashlar, rose sun, facade sun, portico, steps, and lancets survive.
Every structural roof is a closed solid prism or faceted solid; no dual rotated box-slab roof is permitted.
The palette stays bright and clean with geometric relief, no photoreal micro-noise, and no reference-image billboard.

lodPlan.strategy: retain silhouette and solar symbols; reduce ashlar and leading draw calls
merge static masonry and simplify repeated surface relief

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Share geometries/materials and use instancing for masonry, slate, windows, buttresses, radial rays, and spire ribs without deleting identity features.

lightingFromPhoto: Broad warm-neutral key light from upper-front-left at intensity near 2.3 with soft shadows defines gables, ashlar, columns, and spire facets.
Cool-neutral rear-right fill near 0.45 keeps recessed doors, belfry arches, and side lancets readable without flattening contrast.
Subtle hemisphere or rim/environment light near 0.7 separates the dark slate roof and spire from a neutral light-gray background.
Use ACES filmic tone mapping at exposure near 1.0 and a soft contact/ground shadow under the foundation, steps, and portico columns.
proceduralStrategy: Build nave and portico structural roofs as closed indexed gable prisms; never use two rotated boxes as roof slabs.
Build pointed lancets and gable wall profiles with Shape/ExtrudeGeometry, circular solar systems with radial sectors/rays, and the spire as a closed faceted solid.
Use shared deterministic geometry or InstancedMesh for ashlar blocks, slate modules, buttresses, window systems, sun rays, belfry arches, and spire ribs.
Use bright MeshToonMaterial and toon-compatible MeshStandardMaterial families with real geometric seams/chamfers and no image planes.
Expose door hinges, sockets, primitive collider metadata, and semantic destruction groups through root.userData.sculptRuntime.
animationAnchors: left-door-hinge and right-door-hinge sockets support door animation
finial-seat and facade ornament pivots support detachable effects
destructionAnchors: nave-masonry and tower-masonry fracture groups follow ashlar/material seams
rose-glass and lancet-glass groups expose breakable glazing
nave-roof and spire-slate groups detach along existing trim bands
risks: The rear elevation is inferred; keep it restrained.
Too many lead cames can muddy the stylized glass at game distance.
Slate relief must remain visibly subordinate to the solid manifold roof.
